title: Private Equity and Deal Sourcing

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Finding Acquisition Targets
children.blurb: Finding acquisition targets is the process of identifying companies that fit a private equity fund's investment criteria, including sector, size, growth, and ownership structure.

children.name: Data Room Diligence
children.blurb: Data room diligence in private equity and deal sourcing covers the structured review of a target company's documents during due diligence, including financial statements, contracts, customer lists, intellectual property, employment records, litigation and regulatory filings.

children.name: Buyout Modelling
children.blurb: Buyout modelling covers the construction and stress-testing of leveraged buyout financial models, including sources and uses, debt schedules, operating forecasts, and sponsor returns.

children.name: Private Market Valuation
children.blurb: Private market valuation covers the pricing of equity and debt in companies that are not publicly traded, with a focus on AI businesses where traditional financials may be thin and intangible assets dominate.

children.name: Tracking Synergies After a Merger
children.blurb: Tracking synergies after a merger means monitoring whether the combined entity achieves the cost savings, revenue gains, and operational improvements that justified the deal.

sections.body: Private equity and deal sourcing is the part of investing that finds companies to buy, checks them, prices them, and then tries to make the combined business worth more. In AI, this work now uses models to scan filings, patents, hiring data, and product releases for signs of a target. Deal teams use language models to read long documents and flag risks in data rooms, and they use forecasting tools to test buyout assumptions. The work is not fully automated. A model can surface candidates and summarize contracts, but a person still decides whether a business is worth pursuing. The field is about speed and coverage, not about replacing judgment.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are more solved than others. Target screening is fairly mature because public data and filings can be processed at scale, and this site tracks 354 merger and acquisition filings as one source of that activity. Data room diligence is partly solved for search and extraction, but models still miss context, misread tables, and struggle with poor scans. Buyout modelling remains human led because the model depends on assumptions about growth, margins, and debt that no system can validate on its own. Private market valuation is harder than public valuation because comparable transactions are sparse and prices are often not disclosed, and post merger synergy tracking is the least settled, since promised savings are easy to state and hard to measure. The honest limit is that AI can organize evidence, but it cannot confirm that a deal will work.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section follow the deal from search to integration. Finding Acquisition Targets covers how screens and signals narrow a market into a shortlist. Data Room Diligence covers document review, risk flags, and the limits of automated reading. Buyout Modelling covers the spreadsheets and scenario tools that test whether a purchase can be financed and repaid. Private Market Valuation covers the methods used when no public price exists, including comparables and negotiated marks. Tracking Synergies After a Merger covers the follow through, where cost savings and revenue gains are measured against the original case, and a reader can move through the pages in order or jump to the stage that matches the question at hand.
